Subject: PII handling confirmation — prompts & outputs (post-call)

Hi Laura / Tom,

Thanks again for a productive call this morning — appreciate the clear rundown of Acme Health's use case and the sensitivity around patient identifiers and PHI in prompts. To recap the action items and provide the quick confirmation you asked for on what Redwood stores and for how long: 

Summary (hosted Redwood API - default behavior):
- Prompts & outputs: logged for troubleshooting, abuse detection, and traceability for 30 days by default. Logs are encrypted at rest and in transit.
- Training: Redwood does not use customer prompts or outputs to train or improve models without explicit, documented opt-in.
- Audit & access: Access to stored logs is restricted to a small SRE/Support group and is audited.
- Data residency: Data is stored in the region tied to your account (we default to us-west-2 for US accounts). EU accounts can be configured to store logs in eu-west-1.
- Retention adjustments: For Hosted customers we can reduce retention to 0/7/30/90 days via contract/feature flag for certain tiers — Dedicated/Private deployments provide full control over retention.

Recommendations & mitigations we discussed:
- Use the "no-store" header or the dedicated redaction proxy for any prompt fields containing direct identifiers (SSNs, MRNs) to avoid logging.
- Use response masking on the client side for UI displays; avoid storing full outputs in downstream analytics if they contain PHI.
- For high-assurance environments, Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) provides customer-controlled storage and KMS/HSM integration.

Attachments: I attached a short "Data handling & retention summary" PDF that outlines the options above and the default behaviors.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm which retention level you need for the hosted environment (default 30 days or alternate).
2) If you want Redwood to store logs in an EU region, let us know and we'll prepare a region-specific addendum.
3) Neha (cc) — can you confirm the default retention and provide the SOC2 / third-party audit links?

I'll follow up with the security questionnaire and a draft MSA redline checklist once we confirm residency/retention.

Best,

Marissa Cole

Hi all — thanks for the clear questions. Confirming the standard Redwood Hosted behaviors and the options available to Acme Health below.

1) What we store by default:
- Prompts: by default we persist full request payloads (prompts) to access logs for 30 days to support debugging, abuse detection, and billing reconciliation.
- Model outputs: by default we persist full responses to logs for the same 30-day window.
- Metadata: request ids, timestamps, latency, model version, and token counts are retained with the logs.

2) Deletion semantics:
- Default hosted retention (30 days) means data is removed from primary live storage after 30 days. We also run a rolling purge of retention-expired records from backups on a 90-day schedule. If Acme requires stricter guarantees, we can contractually commit to a 30-day permanent deletion window (i.e., remove from active storage and schedule expedited backup purges) — we'll need the addendum in the MSA.

3) Training & product use:
- Under no circumstance do we use customer prompt/output data to train Redwood models unless the customer explicitly opts in via written agreement.

4) Region & residency:
- We support regionally-scoped storage for hosted accounts. Switching an existing account to EU residency typically takes 5-10 business days for onboarding and data-migration steps; yank of users in US may see ~20-40ms additional RTT for EU-hosted logs depending on geography. For strict residency requirements we recommend Redwood Private or Dedicated where storage is fully under customer control.

5) Controls & mitigations:
- API-level "no-store" header to prevent logging of a particular request.
- Redaction proxy / client-side redaction templates for removing identifiers before transit.
- Customer-managed KMS available on Dedicated/Private.

Attached: Acme-specific data handling summary + links to SOC2 report and our data retention addendum template.

Next steps I recommend:
- Laura: confirm desired hosted retention (30 / 7 / 0) and whether you need a contractual addendum for backup purge guarantees.
- If Acme needs EU residency, let us know and we'll open a region-change ticket (5-10 business days).
- I'll share the SOC2 report link and the MSA addendum template in a follow-up secure link (drive link attached).

Neha Kapoor
